subject: English
summaryPoints: Future intentions are distinguished between 'be going to + infinitive' (pre-formulated plans, intentions, or events with present physical evidence) and 'will + infinitive' (spontaneous decisions, predictions without present evidence, promises, and offers).
Present continuous tense expresses actions occurring at the moment of speech, temporary current situations, and annoying habitual behaviors when modified by 'always' or 'constantly'.

Indefinite pronouns 'some' and 'any' follow distribution rules: 'some' is used in affirmative assertions and polite offers/requests expecting an affirmative answer; 'any' is used in negative statements, standard interrogatives, and affirmative statements conveying 'no matter which'.

Clauses of result express outcomes using 'so...that' (followed by an adjective or adverb, or many/much/few/little + noun) and 'such...that' (followed by an adjective + singular countable noun with 'a/an', or adjective + plural/uncountable noun).
Compound nouns are formed through various lexical combinations: noun + noun (toothbrush, school teacher), adjective + noun (greenhouse, black box), and verb + noun (swimming pool, driving license).

Apostrophes mark singular possession before the 's' (girl's book), regular plural possession after the 's' (girls' books), irregular plural possession before the 's' (children's toys), and joint possession on the final noun (Belete and Ayele's book).

formulas.label: Clause of Result with 'So...that'
formulas.expr: Subject + Verb + so + adjective/adverb + that + Clause of Result  OR  so + many/much/few/little + Noun + that + Clause

formulas.label: Clause of Result with 'Such...that'
formulas.expr: Subject + Verb + such + (a/an) + adjective + Noun + that + Clause of Result

formulas.label: Joint vs Individual Possession Formula
formulas.expr: Joint: Noun1 and Noun2's + Noun (shared)  |  Separate: Noun1's and Noun2's + Nouns (separate)

formulas.label: Future Intentions Formula
formulas.expr: Planned/Evidence: Subject + is/am/are + going to + V1  |  Spontaneous/Uncertain: Subject + will + V1

examTip: In EUEE questions testing 'so' versus 'such', remember that 'many', 'much', 'few', and 'little' are always preceded by 'so', never 'such' (e.g., 'so many books', NOT 'such many books'). Conversely, use 'such a/an' when an adjective is followed by a singular countable noun ('such a great teacher').

keyDefinitions.definition: A subordinate clause introduced by conjunctions such as 'so...that' or 'such...that' that expresses the consequence or outcome of an action or condition.
A lexical unit formed by combining two or more distinct words (e.g., noun+noun, adj+noun, verb+noun) that functions syntactically as a single nominal entity.
A pronoun (e.g., some, any, somebody, anywhere) that refers to unspecified, non-particular persons, items, or quantities.
A grammatical relationship indicating that two or more entities share ownership of the same object, marked by attaching an apostrophe -s exclusively to the final noun.

eueeFocusTopics: Selection of 'be going to' (evidence/prior plan) versus 'will' (spontaneous/promise)
